how.intro: Adds a real stop order on SoDEX for every trade, as a safety net if DeskLabs goes offline.
steps: It is placed as soon as the entry fills, 0.1% of the price further away than the bot's own stop loss, so normally the bot's stop acts first.
Once the trade is far enough in profit (see Move stop to break-even), the stop on SoDEX moves to break-even, then follows the price to lock in profit.
how.note: It is triggered by the mark price and closes the whole position at market.

vfEarlyFees.label: Early profit
vfEarlyFees.hint: Exit early once the price gain reaches this many times the round-trip fee (1–20×)

how.intro: Takes a smaller profit early instead of waiting for the full hold time.
steps: After the delay set next to it (seconds), if profit ≥ this × the round-trip fees, the bot closes the trade.
Example: 3× with 10 s → after 10 seconds, any trade that has made 3 times its fees is closed.
how.note: Lower = more small wins, less time exposed. Higher = lets winners run longer.

vfEarlySecs.label: Early profit after
vfEarlySecs.hint: Seconds in the trade before an early exit is allowed

maxOrders.label: Max open position, in orders
maxOrders.hint: How many orders’ worth of position the bot may hold, 1–10. 1 = at most one order size (20 USDC at 20 per side); at the limit the bot only posts the close.

how.intro: Caps how much position the bot may build, as a number of orders: max position = order size per side × this number.
steps: While under the cap, the bot keeps quoting both sides.
With a position open, the side that would add to it moves further away (2–3 ticks back), and the side that closes it stays near the price.
At the cap, the side that would add more stops quoting until the position shrinks.
how.note: Example: 20 USDC per side and 1 order → at most about 20 USDC of position at a time. Higher values give more fills but more price risk.

quoteLevel.label: Quote position in the order book
quoteLevel.hint: 0 = at the best bid and ask (one tick inside when the spread is wide), the fastest fills. 1, 2… = that many price steps behind: fewer fills, less exposure to fast moves. Works the same on every market because it follows the live order book.

how.intro: Sets where your bid and ask sit in the SoDEX order book, counted in ticks (the smallest price step) from the best price.
steps: 0: your bid sits at the best bid and your ask at the best ask. If the gap between them is 3 ticks or more, the bot goes 1 tick inside it to be first in line.
1, 2, 3…: each step moves both quotes 1 tick further from the best price.
Your bid is always below your ask, so the bot never trades with itself.
how.note: Lower = more fills and volume, but more fills right before the price moves against you. Higher = fewer fills and less volume. Because it counts ticks, the same value works on every market.

vfStopMove.label: Move stop to break-even at
vfStopMove.hint: When the price gain reaches this many times the break-even fee (entry fee + market exit fee + slippage), the stop on SoDEX moves to break-even. From 2 more, it locks in profit and follows the best price. Lower moves sooner but small swings can close the trade.

how.intro: When to move the stop on SoDEX to break-even, in multiples of G. G = entry fee + taker exit fee + a little slippage: the price move needed just to cover costs.
steps: Profit reaches this × G: the stop moves to break-even (fees included), so the trade can no longer lose.
Profit reaches (this + 2) × G: the stop locks in profit and follows the best price, 2 × G behind it.
The stop never moves back.
how.note: Lower (e.g. 1–1.5) protects sooner but gets stopped at break-even more often. Higher leaves more room. The current target price is shown in Decisions when the stop is placed.

smartQuoting.label: Smart quoting
smartQuoting.hint: Steps a quote back, or pulls it during a trend, when a fill is likely to be followed by a move against you. Off keeps the classic behaviour exactly.

how.intro: Normally the bot keeps one bid and one ask at the set position in the order book. With Smart quoting on, it watches the book and the last 30 seconds of price, and steps a quote back or pulls it when a fill is likely to be followed by a move against you:
steps: Warm-up: for the first 6 seconds both quotes sit 2 bp further away until there is enough price data.
Lopsided book: one side of the top 10 levels holds at least 2× the other. The thin side steps back 1 bp (e.g. heavy bids → the ask steps back).
Fast move: price moved 2 bp or more in 6 seconds. The quote in the direction of the move steps back 2 bp.
Trend: price moved 5 bp or more in 30 seconds. The quote in the direction of the trend is pulled until it calms down (price rising → no ask).
Every adjustment is kept for 15 seconds after the last trigger, so quotes don't snap back in the middle of a move. Orders that close your inventory are never moved.
how.note: Distances are in bp, so they mean the same on every market. It only ever quotes further away or not at all, never closer, so expect fewer fills and less volume in exchange for fewer bad fills. Works only when quotes follow the order book (Quote level). Each change of action is logged once in Decisions, and Market Making Analytics compares fills with Smart quoting on and off. Beta: thresholds may change.

riskDisclosure.warnTitle: Read this before you start a bot.
riskDisclosure.warnBody: Every DeskLabs bot trades real funds on SoDEX mainnet. You can lose part or all of the money a bot uses, and with leverage you can lose it fast. Only use money you can afford to lose.

loss.title: Real money, real losses
loss.body: Digital asset prices move quickly and without warning. An automated bot follows its rules whatever the market does: it keeps buying in a falling market or selling in a rising one if that is what its settings say. DeskLabs does not guarantee any profit and does not predict prices.

leverage.title: Leverage and liquidation
leverage.body: Futures Grid, Futures DCA, Funding Arbitrage and perps TWAP use perpetual contracts. With leverage, a small price move against you becomes a large loss. If your margin falls below SoDEX’s maintenance requirement, SoDEX can liquidate your position. A liquidation happens on SoDEX and DeskLabs cannot stop or reverse it.

margin.title: Multi-Asset Margin
margin.body: In cross margin, SoDEX counts non-USDC assets as margin at a collateral ratio below 100%, so they are worth less as margin than their full value. Losses are settled in USDC. Your USDC balance can go negative, and an account can be liquidated even without an open position. Isolated margin uses USDC only. The Portfolio page shows how much of your balance counts as margin.

sharedLeverage.title: Shared leverage per market
sharedLeverage.body: On SoDEX, leverage and margin mode are set per account and per market. When a bot sets leverage on a market, it changes it for your whole account, including trades you place yourself. DeskLabs blocks the start when that would affect an open position, and asks you to confirm otherwise.

items.grid: Grid: if price leaves your range, the grid has no levels left to trade and you hold what it bought, or the short it opened, at a loss.
items.dca: DCA: extra buys add to a losing position. A long fall uses all of them and the loss grows with every one.
items.recurring: Recurring Buy: keeps buying on schedule and never sells, whatever the price.
items.rebalancing: Rebalancing: sells assets that rose and buys ones that fell; in a long trend this can lag simply holding.
items.funding: Funding Arbitrage: funding rates change and can turn negative; the spot and perp legs can drift apart; the perp leg can be liquidated.
items.twap: TWAP: slices still pay the spread and can fill at worse prices than when you started.

backtest.title: Backtests and suggestions
backtest.body: A backtest replays SoDEX price history with modeled fills. It is a simulation, not a forecast, and real fills, fees and slippage differ. Strategy plans and AI parameters come from rule-based software reading your data. They are not advice and can be wrong for future markets.

items.offline: SoDEX, networks or DeskLabs can be slow or offline. Bots may miss orders, and open orders stay on SoDEX while that lasts.
items.unknown: When an order’s result is unknown, DeskLabs checks with SoDEX before acting again, which can delay the bot.
items.key: If your SoDEX connection expires or stops working, bots pause until you reconnect.
items.bugs: Software can have bugs. Server-enforced risk limits reduce, but do not remove, that risk.

items.botLimits: Set a max loss and stop price on each bot, and keep leverage low.

spot_grid.what: Places buy orders below the price and sell orders above it, and earns small gains as the price moves up and down.

futures_grid.what: Works like a grid on a perpetual, using leverage. Gains and losses are both larger.

spot_dca.what: Buys, then buys more as the price drops, and sells the whole position at a take-profit.
spot_dca.lose: A long fall uses every extra buy and can reach the loss limit.

futures_dca.what: Adds to a perpetual position as the price moves against it, then takes profit. Uses leverage.
futures_dca.lose: A trend that keeps going can hit the stop loss. Funding fees also apply.

recurring_buy.what: Buys a small amount every week, whatever the price. It never sells.
recurring_buy.lose: If the price falls for a long time, your holdings fall with it.

rebalancing.what: Keeps your coins at a fixed mix by trimming what grew and adding to what fell.
rebalancing.lose: If all your coins fall together, your total value falls too.

funding_arb.what: Holds the coin and an equal perpetual short to collect funding payments.
funding_arb.lose: Funding turns negative, or the two sides drift apart before the bot closes them.

will.spot_grid: It splits {capital} USDC into buy and sell orders between {lower} and {upper}. It buys when the price falls and sells when it rises. It stops if the price drops below {stop}, or near a {maxLoss} USDC loss.

will.futures_dca: It opens a {leverage}× long on {market} with {base} USDC, adds up to {count} more orders of {safety} USDC as the price drops, and takes profit {tp}% above the average price. It closes at a {sl}% loss, or near a {maxLoss} USDC loss.
will.recurring_buy: It buys {amount} USDC of {market} every week, {count} times. It never sells.
will.rebalancing: It keeps {capital} USDC split as {weights}, and trades back when a weight drifts by more than {threshold}%.
